Subject: Aligning MAP milestones with legal signature window — handoff & fallback choreography

Hi Ellie —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that ties the technical evaluation milestones to the legal/procurement milestones you mentioned (MSA review, DPA comments, and order form approval).

High level ask: can your procurement team confirm the earliest order-form signing window they have in March/April given internal approvals? That helps us avoid a final-week scramble if the DPA redlines come late. I sketched two fallback paths in the MAP:
- Path A (preferred): MSA and DPA sign-off ahead of order-form approval; deploy pilot in reserved capacity
- Path B (fallback): Bind via temporary PO + interim data protection addendum while DPA iteration completes

Attachments: CurePath_MAP_v1.xlsx, MSA_DPA_Signature_Windows.pdf

Next steps I propose:
1) You share procurement constraints (calendar blackout dates, stakeholder approvers) by EOD Friday
2) Laura and Marcus will review the MAP and call out any legal edge cases related to data residency or audit logs by Monday
3) We set a 30-minute cadence next week to triage any DPA redlines so the MAP stays current

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor

Neha —

Appreciate the map, this is helpful. A couple quick notes from procurement side:
- We have an internal board review on 2026-03-25 that is effectively a hard cutoff for any contracts needing Q2 spend approval. Anything after that slips to the next monthly finance cycle (mid-April).
- Our legal ops person (Tom) will own DPA redlines; he asked if you can flag any clauses that are likely to trigger an escalated review (data export, subprocessors, breach notification timelines).
- PO-as-temp-binding is possible but will need signoff from Finance; lead time for that is ~5 business days.

Tom / procurement team — we can use the Path B sketch if DPA redlines push us past the board cutoff, but we need concrete timeline commitments from Redwood on how fast the DPA iterations will turn around.

Ellie

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ellie Summers <esummers@curepath.com>, Tom Ellis <tellis@curepath.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning MAP milestones with legal signature window — handoff & fallback choreography

Folks —

Reviewed the MAP and the two-path approach looks solid. A few legal flags to call out that should be surfaced in the shared doc so procurement and their counsel can see the vectors:
1) Data residency carve-outs — if CurePath needs EU-only processing for any PHI in the pilot, that changes our hosting configuration and will push the technical onboarding by ~7 business days.
2) Subprocessor list cadence — our standard DPA requires 30 days notice for new subprocessors; if CurePath needs an accelerated addendum please let us know.
3) SLA/credits on model availability — we can provide a pilot SLO but production SLA and escrow obligations need executive approval and will not be in scope for the initial PO.

To reduce friction I recommend we: 
- Mark the MAP with explicit acceptance gates (legal, security, procurement) and a single owner for each gate; that prevents the ambiguous "legal review" handoff.
- Set an internal SLAT (legal turnaround) of 3 business days per redline during the onramp week — we'll commit to that for prioritized issues.

If procurement confirms the board review on 2026-03-25, then Path A requires DPA finalization by 2026-03-18 to allow signature routing. Path B is viable up until 2026-03-23 if Finance approves a PO buffer.

Happy to jump on a call with CurePath counsel if that will speed alignment.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com

Quick timeline proposal to operationalize Path A and Path B. Table form in text:

Week 0 (Mar 8–12): Redwood finalizes MAP updates with legal flags annotated (Neha / Laura) — commit to 3-business-day turnaround per redline for prioritized items.
Week 1 (Mar 15–19): CurePath completes internal technical eval and surfaces any open export/subprocessor asks. Redwood provides DPA edit pass within 48–72 hours.
Week 2 (Mar 22–26): Final DPA routing; if signed by 3/25 (board review), Path A proceeds to order-form signature and pilot setup. If not, trigger Path B: PO buffer requested by 3/23 and interim DPA addendum executed by Redwood and CurePath counsel.

Operational notes:
- Owner assignments: Legal gate (Laura), Procurement gate (Neha), Tech gate (Marcus).
- Escalation: if DPA redline requires C-suite review, notify Neha + Rishi immediately and we will route to EVP for approval within 24 hours.

I can convert this into a one-page MAP summary (GDrive link) and a short checklist for the CurePath procurement team. If procurement confirms board date and PO window today, we'll iterate the MAP and share v1.1 by EOD.
